board_events.text: Part (a). Convert the energy per fission into joules first, so that it matches the units of power.
Part (b). Scale up to a full day, then convert a number of nuclei into grams using Avogadro's number.
Answer: about $9.4 \times 10^{18}$ fissions per second, consuming roughly 0.32 kg per day. The fuel loaded is far larger, since only the fissile fraction is consumed.

segments.text: The previous example went from a mass of fuel to an energy. This one runs the same chain of logic in the opposite direction, from a power output back to a mass of fuel. Recognising that it is the same logic reversed is most of the battle.
The board lays out the three steps. Power in joules per second, divided by joules per fission, gives fissions per second. Then fissions per day, converted through Avogadro, gives grams.

Part a. The first move is a unit conversion, and getting it right early prevents everything downstream from going wrong. Power is given in megawatts, which is joules per second, but the energy per fission is in mega electron volts. Convert the fission energy to joules first.
Two hundred mega electron volts times one point six times ten to the minus thirteen gives three point two times ten to the minus eleven joules per fission.

Now divide. Three hundred megawatts is three point zero times ten to the eight joules every second. Divide that by three point two times ten to the minus eleven joules per fission, and you need about nine point four times ten to the eighteen fissions every second.
Part b. Scale that up to a full day by multiplying by eighty six thousand four hundred seconds, and then turn a number of nuclei into a mass using Avogadro's number.

Nine point four times ten to the eighteen per second, times eighty six thousand four hundred, gives about eight point one times ten to the twenty three fissions in a day. Notice that this is close to Avogadro's number, which means we are dealing with roughly one mole of uranium.
Divide by Avogadro's number to get the number of moles, and multiply by two hundred and thirty five grams per mole. That gives about three hundred and sixteen grams.

<excited>So a three hundred megawatt station, powering a whole city, consumes about a third of a kilogram of uranium-two-three-five per day. One honest caveat the chapter adds: the fuel actually loaded into the reactor is far larger than this, because only the fissile fraction of the fuel is consumed. But the physics number is what it is, and it is remarkable.
पिछला example fuel के mass से energy तक गया था। यह वही तर्क उल्टी दिशा में चलाता है, power output से वापस fuel के mass तक। यह पहचान लेना कि यह वही तर्क उल्टा है, आधी लड़ाई है।
Board तीनों steps रख रहा है। Power joule प्रति second में, बटा joule प्रति fission, देता है fissions प्रति second। फिर fissions प्रति दिन, Avogadro से गुज़रकर, देता है grams।

Part a। पहला कदम एक unit conversion है, और इसे शुरू में ही ठीक कर लेने से आगे का सब कुछ बचा रहता है। Power megawatts में दी है, यानी joule प्रति second, पर energy per fission mega electron volts में है। पहले fission energy को joules में बदलिए।
दो सौ mega electron volts into one point six into ten to the minus thirteen देता है three point two into ten to the minus eleven joule प्रति fission।

अब भाग दीजिए। तीन सौ megawatt यानी three point zero into ten to the eight joule हर second। इसे three point two into ten to the minus eleven joule प्रति fission से भाग दीजिए, तो हर second लगभग nine point four into ten to the eighteen fissions चाहिए।
Part b। इसे पूरे दिन तक बढ़ाइए, छियासी हज़ार चार सौ second से गुणा करके, और फिर nuclei की संख्या को Avogadro number से mass में बदलिए।

Nine point four into ten to the eighteen प्रति second, into छियासी हज़ार चार सौ, देता है एक दिन में लगभग eight point one into ten to the twenty three fissions। ध्यान दीजिए यह Avogadro number के काफी पास है, यानी हम लगभग एक mole uranium की बात कर रहे हैं।
Avogadro number से भाग देकर moles निकालिए, और दो सौ पैंतीस gram प्रति mole से गुणा कीजिए। मिलता है लगभग तीन सौ सोलह gram।

<excited>तो तीन सौ megawatt का station, जो एक पूरे शहर को बिजली देता है, रोज़ लगभग एक तिहाई kilogram uranium-two-three-five खर्च करता है। Chapter एक ईमानदार बात जोड़ता है: reactor में असल में भरा गया fuel इससे कहीं ज़्यादा होता है, क्योंकि उसका सिर्फ fissile हिस्सा ही खर्च होता है। पर physics का number जो है सो है, और वो हैरान करने वाला है।

sections.subtopic: Nuclear Energy: Fission, Fusion, and the Power of the Stars
sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips: fission, fusion and reactors

board_events.text: Four pitfalls in nuclear energy
1. Thinking fast neutrons are best for fission.
Uranium-235 fissions most readily with slow, thermal neutrons, which is exactly why a moderator exists. Mixing up the moderator's and control rods' jobs is the most common reactor mistake.
2. Believing fusion is 'easier' because the nuclei are small.
Small nuclei still carry positive charge. The Coulomb barrier makes fusion harder to ignite than fission, despite the larger energy yield per nucleon.
3. Sign errors in the Q-value.
Q is reactant masses minus product masses, times c squared. If your products are heavier, Q is negative and energy must be supplied. Do not force a positive answer.
4. Forgetting to convert MeV to joules, or mixing per-fission with per-gram quantities.
Track your units explicitly on every line. Most lost marks in this subtopic are unit slips, not physics errors.

Pro-tip: for 'energy from m grams', find the number of nuclei first, then multiply by the per-event energy. For reactor power, run it the other way: divide the power by the per-fission energy to get the fission rate.

segments.text: Four pitfalls to close the subtopic, and unusually for this chapter, two of them are conceptual traps and two are pure carelessness. The careless ones cost just as many marks.
Pitfall one, and it is the single most tested misconception in this subtopic. Thinking that fast neutrons are best for causing fission.

They are not. Uranium-two-three-five fissions most readily with slow, thermal neutrons, and that is the entire reason a moderator exists inside a reactor. The closely related error is swapping the jobs of the moderator and the control rods, which is the most common reactor mistake of all. Moderator slows; control rods absorb.
Pitfall two. Believing that fusion must be easier than fission because the nuclei involved are so small.

Small nuclei still carry positive charge, and that is what matters. The Coulomb barrier makes fusion much harder to ignite than fission, despite fusion having the larger energy yield per nucleon. Higher yield and easier to achieve are two completely different claims, and only the first is true of fusion.
Pitfall three, sign errors in the Q-value, which is the carelessness that produces confident wrong answers.

Q is reactant masses minus product masses, times c squared, in that order. If your products come out heavier, then Q is genuinely negative, the reaction is endothermic, and energy must be supplied from outside. Do not flip the subtraction to force a positive answer just because the question said 'energy released'.
Pitfall four. Forgetting to convert mega electron volts into joules, or mixing per-fission quantities with per-gram quantities halfway through a calculation.

The remedy is unhelpfully simple but genuinely works: track your units explicitly on every single line. Most of the marks lost in this subtopic are unit slips rather than physics errors, which makes them the cheapest marks to recover.

<whisper>And the pro-tip, which is really one piece of logic used in two directions. For 'energy from m grams' questions, find the number of nuclei first, then multiply by the per-event energy. For reactor power questions, run exactly the same chain backwards: divide the power by the per-fission energy to get the fission rate, then convert to mass. Same chain of logic, opposite direction.
Subtopic बंद करने के लिए चार pitfalls, और इस chapter के लिए असामान्य रूप से, दो conceptual traps हैं और दो पूरी तरह लापरवाही। लापरवाही वाले भी उतने ही marks ले जाते हैं।
Pitfall one, और यह इस subtopic की सबसे ज़्यादा पूछी जाने वाली गलतफ़हमी है। यह सोचना कि fission कराने के लिए fast neutrons सबसे अच्छे हैं।

वो नहीं हैं। Uranium-two-three-five slow, thermal neutrons से सबसे आसानी से fission होता है, और reactor में moderator होने की पूरी वजह यही है। इससे जुड़ी गलती है moderator और control rods के काम आपस में बदल देना, जो सबसे आम reactor गलती है। Moderator धीमा करता है; control rods सोखते हैं।
Pitfall two। यह मानना कि fusion fission से आसान होगा क्योंकि उसमें शामिल nuclei इतने छोटे हैं।

छोटे nuclei पर भी positive charge है, और अहम यही है। Coulomb barrier fusion को fission से कहीं ज़्यादा मुश्किल बना देता है, जबकि per nucleon fusion की yield ज़्यादा है। ज़्यादा yield और आसानी से हासिल होना, दो बिल्कुल अलग दावे हैं, और fusion के बारे में सिर्फ़ पहला सही है।
Pitfall three, Q-value में sign की गलतियाँ, और यही वो लापरवाही है जो आत्मविश्वास से भरे गलत जवाब पैदा करती है।

Q है reactant masses minus product masses, into c squared, इसी क्रम में। अगर आपके products भारी निकलते हैं, तो Q सचमुच negative है, reaction endothermic है, और energy बाहर से देनी पड़ेगी। सिर्फ इसलिए subtraction उल्टा मत कीजिए कि question में 'energy released' लिखा था।
Pitfall four। Mega electron volts को joules में बदलना भूल जाना, या calculation के बीच में per fission और per gram राशियों को आपस में मिला देना।

इलाज बेकार जितना आसान है पर सचमुच काम करता है: हर एक line पर units साफ़ लिखते चलिए। इस subtopic में गँवाए गए ज़्यादातर marks unit की चूक होते हैं, physics की गलती नहीं, और इसीलिए ये सबसे सस्ते में वापस पाए जा सकने वाले marks हैं।

<whisper>और pro-tip, जो असल में एक ही तर्क दो दिशाओं में है। 'M gram से energy' वाले questions में पहले nuclei की संख्या निकालिए, फिर per event energy से गुणा कीजिए। Reactor power वाले questions में ठीक वही chain उल्टी चलाइए: power को per fission energy से भाग देकर fission rate निकालिए, फिर mass में बदलिए। वही तर्क, उल्टी दिशा।

sections.subtopic: Chapter Close: Formula Recap and Cheat Sheet
sections.title: Formula recap: your complete toolkit for Nuclei

board_events.text: Every formula in this chapter, on one board

board_events.latex: R = R_0 A^{1/3},\ R_0 \approx 1.2\ \text{fm} \qquad \rho = \frac{m_N}{\tfrac{4}{3}\pi R_0^{3}} \approx 2.3 \times 10^{17}\ \text{kg m}^{-3}
\Delta m = \left[Z m_{\mathrm{H}} + (A-Z) m_n\right] - M_{\text{atom}} \qquad E_b = \Delta m \times 931.5\ \text{MeV}
\frac{E_b}{A}: \text{ peaks at } \approx 8.8\ \text{MeV near } A = 56; \ \approx 7.6\ \text{MeV at uranium}
N = N_0 e^{-\lambda t} \qquad N = \frac{N_0}{2^{\,n}},\ n = \frac{t}{T_{1/2}}
\alpha: A-4,\ Z-2 \qquad \beta^{-}: A,\ Z+1 \qquad \beta^{+}: A,\ Z-1 \qquad \gamma: \text{no change}

segments.text: This is your complete toolkit for the chapter, gathered onto one board. I am not going to re-teach any of it. I am simply going to walk the list, so that you know what should be at your fingertips before a paper.

Nuclear size and density. Radius equals R nought A to the one third, with R nought about one point two femtometres. And the density, which contains no A at all, about two point three times ten to the seventeen kilograms per cubic metre.

The mass-energy group. The atomic mass unit in kilograms, Einstein's relation, and the bridge you will actually use: one atomic mass unit corresponds to nine hundred and thirty one point five mega electron volts.
Mass defect and binding energy. Constituents by the neutral-atom route, minus the measured atomic mass, then multiplied by nine hundred and thirty one point five.
The two numbers off the binding-energy curve. It peaks near eight point eight mega electron volts per nucleon around mass number fifty six, and has fallen to about seven point six by uranium.
The decay law in both forms. The exponential for any time at all, and the halving form for whole numbers of half-lives.
Half-life and mean life, with the relation between them. Zero point six nine three over lambda, one over lambda, and the factor one point four four connecting them.
Activity and its units. Activity equals lambda N and decays exponentially like everything else, with one curie being three point seven times ten to the ten becquerel.
The displacement laws in compressed form. Alpha takes four off A and two off Z. Beta minus leaves A and adds one to Z. Beta plus leaves A and takes one off Z. Gamma changes neither.

<whisper>And the energy line. Q equals the mass defect times nine hundred and thirty one point five, with the three reaction energies worth knowing cold: about two hundred mega electron volts per fission, seventeen point six for deuterium-tritium, and twenty six point seven for the proton-proton cycle. If you can reproduce this board from memory, you can attempt any question in this chapter.
यह पूरे chapter का आपका complete toolkit है, एक ही board पर इकट्ठा। मैं इनमें से कुछ भी दोबारा नहीं पढ़ाऊँगा। मैं बस list पर चलूँगा, ताकि आपको पता रहे कि paper से पहले क्या उँगलियों पर होना चाहिए।

Nuclear size और density। Radius बराबर R nought A to the one third, R nought लगभग one point two femtometre। और density, जिसमें A है ही नहीं, लगभग two point three into ten to the seventeen kilogram per cubic metre।
Mass-energy वाला समूह। Atomic mass unit kilogram में, Einstein का relation, और वो bridge जो आप सचमुच इस्तेमाल करेंगे: एक atomic mass unit बराबर nine hundred thirty one point five mega electron volts।
Mass defect और binding energy। Neutral-atom रास्ते से constituents, minus मापा गया atomic mass, फिर nine hundred thirty one point five से गुणा।
Binding-energy curve से दो numbers। यह mass number छप्पन के आसपास लगभग eight point eight mega electron volts per nucleon पर peak करती है, और uranium तक गिरकर लगभग seven point six रह जाती है।
Decay law दोनों रूपों में। किसी भी समय के लिए exponential, और पूरी half-lives के लिए halving वाला रूप।
Half-life और mean life, और दोनों का रिश्ता। Zero point six nine three बटा lambda, one बटा lambda, और उन्हें जोड़ने वाला factor one point four four।
Activity और उसकी units। Activity बराबर lambda N, और बाकी सबकी तरह exponentially घटती है, और एक curie बराबर three point seven into ten to the ten becquerel।
Displacement laws छोटे रूप में। Alpha A से चार और Z से दो घटाता है। Beta minus A को छोड़ता है और Z में एक जोड़ता है। Beta plus A को छोड़ता है और Z से एक घटाता है। Gamma दोनों में से कुछ नहीं बदलता।

<whisper>और energy वाली line। Q बराबर mass defect into nine hundred thirty one point five, और तीन reaction energies पक्की याद होनी चाहिए: प्रति fission लगभग दो सौ mega electron volts, deuterium-tritium के लिए seventeen point six, और proton-proton cycle के लिए twenty six point seven। अगर आप यह board याद से बना सकें, तो इस chapter का कोई भी question हल कर सकते हैं।

board_events.text: Notation and families: A above, Z below, N = A - Z. Isotopes same Z, isobars same A, isotones same N. Mnemonic: Proton, A-equals-bar, Neutron.
Size and density: radius ratio is the cube root of the A-ratio; density ratio is always 1 to 1. Nuclear matter is about $10^{14}$ times denser than water.
Mass-energy: 1 u is 931.5 MeV. Rest energies: electron 0.511 MeV, proton 938.3 MeV, neutron 939.6 MeV.
Binding energy: the mass defect is always positive. Per-nucleon is the stability measure, peaking near iron. Energy released = BE of products minus BE of reactants.
Nuclear force: strongest in its domain, short-range, charge-independent, saturating, with a repulsive core below about 0.7 fm.
Radioactivity: half-life is independent of sample size; mean life is the longer one at 1.44 times half-life; activity falls by the same factor as N.
Nuclear energy: fission needs slow neutrons and gives about 200 MeV; k = 1 is a reactor; fusion needs about $10^{7}$ K and wins per nucleon.
One-liners: volume scales with A, so radius takes the cube root and density does not scale at all. Per-nucleon is the king of stability, and everyone climbs toward iron.

segments.text: Last section of the chapter, and this is the one to come back to the night before a paper. Nothing new, just the highest-value line from each part of the chapter.
The map shows how the four subtopics connect, and it is worth seeing them as one story rather than four topics. Size leads to binding, binding leads to decay, decay leads to energy.

Notation and families first. Mass number above, atomic number below, neutron number the difference. Isotopes hold Z, isobars hold A, isotones hold N. And the mnemonic for the order: Proton, A-equals-bar, Neutron.

Size and density. For a radius ratio, cube-root the mass-number ratio. For a density ratio, the answer is one to one without any calculation. And for scale, nuclear matter is around ten to the fourteen times denser than water.

The mass-energy bridge, and the three rest energies that show up as distractors in multiple choice questions. One atomic mass unit is nine hundred and thirty one point five mega electron volts. The electron is zero point five one one, the proton nine hundred and thirty eight point three, the neutron nine hundred and thirty nine point six.

Binding energy. The mass defect is always positive. The per-nucleon value, not the total, is what measures stability, and it peaks near iron. And for any reaction where binding energies are given, energy released is simply the binding energy of the products minus that of the reactants.
The nuclear force, as a five-item list. Strongest in its domain, short-range, charge-independent, saturating, and with a repulsive core below about zero point seven femtometres.

Radioactivity, and the three facts that carry the most traps. Half-life is independent of sample size. Mean life is the longer one, at one point four four times the half-life. And activity falls by exactly the same factor as the number of nuclei.

Nuclear energy. Fission needs slow neutrons and yields about two hundred mega electron volts. A multiplication factor of exactly one is a reactor. Fusion needs temperatures of order ten to the seven kelvin and wins on energy per nucleon.

<whisper>And finally the two one-liners that carry the most physics for the fewest words. Volume scales with A, so the radius takes the cube root and the density does not scale at all. And, per-nucleon is the king of stability, and everyone climbs toward iron. That is the chapter.
Chapter का आखिरी section, और paper से एक रात पहले लौटने के लिए यही है। कुछ नया नहीं, बस chapter के हर हिस्से से सबसे कीमती line।
Map दिखा रहा है कि चारों subtopics कैसे जुड़ते हैं, और इन्हें चार topics के बजाय एक कहानी की तरह देखना चाहिए। Size से binding, binding से decay, decay से energy।
पहले notation और families। ऊपर mass number, नीचे atomic number, और neutron number दोनों का अंतर। Isotopes Z पकड़ते हैं, isobars A, isotones N। और क्रम का mnemonic: Proton, A-equals-bar, Neutron।

Size और density। Radius ratio के लिए mass number ratio का cube root लीजिए। Density ratio के लिए जवाब बिना किसी calculation के one to one है। और scale समझिए, nuclear matter पानी से लगभग ten to the fourteen गुना घना है।

Mass-energy bridge, और वो तीन rest energies जो multiple choice में distractors बनकर आती हैं। एक atomic mass unit बराबर nine hundred thirty one point five mega electron volts। Electron zero point five one one, proton nine hundred thirty eight point three, neutron nine hundred thirty nine point six।

Binding energy। Mass defect हमेशा positive होता है। Stability total नहीं, per nucleon वाली value नापती है, और वो iron के पास peak करती है। और जिस भी reaction में binding energies दी हों, released energy बस products की binding energy minus reactants की।
Nuclear force, पाँच बिंदुओं की list के रूप में। अपने इलाके में सबसे ताकतवर, short-range, charge-independent, saturating, और लगभग zero point seven femtometre से नीचे repulsive core के साथ।

Radioactivity, और वो तीन तथ्य जिनमें सबसे ज़्यादा traps हैं। Half-life sample के आकार से स्वतंत्र है। Mean life लंबी होती है, half-life की one point four four गुना। और activity ठीक उसी factor से गिरती है जिससे nuclei की संख्या।

Nuclear energy। Fission को slow neutrons चाहिए और वो लगभग दो सौ mega electron volts देता है। Multiplication factor ठीक एक यानी reactor। Fusion को ten to the seven kelvin के आसपास तापमान चाहिए और per nucleon energy में वो जीतता है।

<whisper>और आखिर में वो दो one-liners जो सबसे कम शब्दों में सबसे ज़्यादा physics ढोती हैं। Volume A के साथ बढ़ता है, इसलिए radius cube root लेता है और density बिल्कुल नहीं बदलती। और, stability का राजा per nucleon है, और सब iron की तरफ चढ़ रहे हैं। यही है यह chapter।
